_meta.warning: SYNTHETIC DEMO DATA. This is not a real drug label. Brand name, generic name, trial names and all numeric results are invented for a hackathon demo. Do not use for any clinical purpose.

agent.role: Answers clinical questions about a single product, grounded only in that product's label and trial data.

product.mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits SGLT2 in the proximal renal tubule, reducing glucose reabsorption and increasing urinary glucose excretion. Produces natriuresis and restores tubuloglomerular feedback, lowering intraglomerular pressure — the presumed basis of its kidney-protective effect independent of glycemic lowering.

indications.detail: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with T2DM.

To reduce the risk of sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with CKD at risk of progression. Benefit demonstrated with and without type 2 diabetes.
To reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with heart failure, across the ejection fraction spectrum.

dosing.standard: 10 mg orally once daily, taken in the morning with or without food.
titration: For glycemic control in T2DM, may increase to 25 mg once daily in patients tolerating 10 mg who require additional A1c lowering and have eGFR >= 45 mL/min/1.73m2.
For the CKD and heart failure indications, 10 mg once daily is the studied and recommended dose. Do not up-titrate for these indications.
renal_adjustment: eGFR 25 to 44: 10 mg once daily. Glycemic efficacy is attenuated; kidney and cardiovascular benefit is retained.
eGFR 20 to 24: do not initiate for glycemic control. Initiation is permitted for the CKD indication. 10 mg once daily.
eGFR < 20: do not initiate. In patients already established on therapy, Renavex may be continued until initiation of dialysis or transplantation.
dosing.hepatic_adjustment: No dose adjustment for mild or moderate hepatic impairment. Not studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C); use is not recommended.
administration_notes: An expected acute dip in eGFR of 3 to 6 mL/min/1.73m2 occurs in the first 2 to 4 weeks. This is hemodynamic, reverses on discontinuation, and predicts long-term benefit. Do not discontinue for this dip alone.
Recheck renal function at 4 weeks after initiation, then per usual CKD monitoring cadence.

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to glifozastat or any component of the formulation.
Type 1 diabetes mellitus — not indicated; substantially elevated diabetic ketoacidosis risk.

warnings_precautions.detail: Ketoacidosis can occur at blood glucose levels below 250 mg/dL, which delays recognition. Risk is elevated with insulin dose reduction, acute illness, prolonged fasting, surgery, very low carbohydrate intake, or alcohol excess. Withhold for at least 3 days before scheduled surgery and during acute illness or prolonged fasting.
Increased incidence of vulvovaginal candidiasis and balanitis, driven by glycosuria. Highest risk in patients with prior episodes and in uncircumcised males.
Increased rate of UTI reported; rare cases of pyelonephritis and urosepsis. Patients with recurrent or complicated UTI warrant a deliberate risk-benefit discussion and closer follow-up.

warnings_precautions.warning: Necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier gangrene)
warnings_precautions.detail: Rare but life-threatening. Evaluate urgently for any perineal pain, tenderness, erythema or swelling with fever or malaise.

Osmotic diuresis may cause intravascular volume contraction, particularly in patients on loop diuretics, patients over 75, and those with eGFR < 45. Assess volume status before initiation; consider reducing loop diuretic dose in euvolemic patients.
Renavex alone rarely causes hypoglycemia. When combined with insulin or an insulin secretagogue, a dose reduction of the insulin or sulfonylurea may be required.

adverse_events.discontinuation_rate: 4.2% due to adverse events vs 3.6% placebo

drug_interactions.effect: Additive diuresis and volume depletion risk.
drug_interactions.management: Assess volume status; consider loop diuretic dose reduction at initiation.
Consider reducing insulin or sulfonylurea dose when initiating.

drug_interactions.effect: May decrease serum lithium concentrations via increased renal clearance.
drug_interactions.management: Monitor lithium levels more frequently after initiation and discontinuation.
Consider 25 mg dose if used for glycemic control and eGFR permits. No change for CKD/HF indication.

pivotal_trials.name: RENAL-GUARD
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled event-driven outcomes trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with CKD, eGFR 25 to 75 mL/min/1.73m2, UACR 200 to 5000 mg/g, on maximally tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB. 67% with type 2 diabetes.
pivotal_trials.primary_endpoint: Composite of sustained >= 50% eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, or renal/cardiovascular death

results.primary: HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.72), p < 0.001. 39% relative risk reduction. Absolute event rate 9.2% vs 14.5%.

subgroups: Benefit consistent with and without type 2 diabetes (p-interaction 0.24).
Benefit consistent across eGFR strata including the 25 to 44 subgroup.
Greater absolute benefit at higher baseline UACR.
limitations: Only 4% of participants had eGFR < 25 at baseline; evidence in advanced CKD is extrapolated.
Trial required UACR >= 200 mg/g. Patients with non-albuminuric CKD were not studied.
Median follow-up 2.4 years; durability beyond 3 years is not established.

pivotal_trials.name: CARDIO-SHIELD
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcomes trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and either established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (41%) or multiple CV risk factors (59%).
pivotal_trials.primary_endpoint: 3-point MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke)

results.primary: HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.84-1.03). Non-inferior to placebo; superiority not met.

subgroups: Heart failure benefit consistent regardless of baseline heart failure history.
Glycemic effect attenuated at eGFR < 45; cardiorenal effect preserved.
limitations: Did not demonstrate MACE superiority. Cardiovascular benefit is driven by heart failure hospitalization and renal endpoints, not atherothrombotic events.
Enrolled patients with A1c 7.0 to 10.5%; effect outside this range is uncharacterized.

monitoring: Renal function and electrolytes at baseline, 4 weeks after initiation, then at least annually (more often at eGFR < 45).
UACR at baseline and at least annually for the CKD indication.
Volume status and blood pressure, especially in the first month and in patients on loop diuretics.
Patient education on DKA symptoms and on sick-day rules (hold during acute illness, fasting, or before surgery).
A1c every 3 months until at goal, then every 6 months.

special_populations.pregnancy: Not recommended in the second and third trimesters. Animal data show adverse renal development effects. Discontinue when pregnancy is recognized.
special_populations.lactation: Not recommended; potential effect on the developing neonatal kidney.
special_populations.pediatric: Safety and effectiveness not established below age 18.
special_populations.geriatric: No dose adjustment. Patients over 75 have higher rates of volume depletion; assess volume status and consider diuretic adjustment.
special_populations.type_1_diabetes: Not indicated. Substantially elevated DKA risk.

strengths: Strongest kidney outcome data of the available options in albuminuric CKD.
Consistent heart failure hospitalization benefit, including in patients without diabetes.
Once-daily oral dosing; no injection burden; no titration schedule for the cardiorenal indication.
limitations: Modest A1c lowering, roughly 0.6 to 0.8%, and attenuated further at low eGFR.
Modest weight loss, roughly 2 to 3 kg.
Did not meet MACE superiority; not the agent to pick when atherothrombotic risk reduction is the primary goal.
Genital mycotic infection and UTI risk is a real tolerability barrier for some patients.

cost_access.tier: Preferred brand on most commercial formularies; Tier 3 on several Medicare Part D plans.
cost_access.prior_authorization: Typically not required for the CKD indication when UACR documentation is present.
cost_access.patient_assistance: Copay card available for commercially insured patients (synthetic).
